Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
15 October 2026 .
Brent $ 105.76 -0.19 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 Gulf oil is still flowing despite a surge in attacks on ships, the New York Times reports.

02 The Washington Post reports Iranian attacks have sunk two ships in the Strait of Hormuz, a story reported on October 14.

03 Brent stood at $105.76, down 0.19% over 24 hours, as of 15:15 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, yet the New York Times reports that Gulf oil is still flowing despite a surge in attacks on ships. The Washington Post reports Iranian attacks sank two ships in the strait, a story reported on October 14. ABC News reports that attacks in the strait have reached their highest daily level since the war began. Iranian state media claim the Iranian Army Navy spotted a burning oil tanker attempting to pass through the eastern strait, though that report originates with Iranian state media and carries no corroboration in this feed. WANA News Agency reports another oil tanker caught fire east of the strait; marketscreener.com carries a headline to the same effect. Fox News and The Lufkin Daily News report containers are floating at sea after a vessel sank near the strait. Al Jazeera and The Guardian report a vessel sank near the strait with containers floating in the water. Bloomberg.com and CNN report a Singapore-registered container ship went down after a strike. Regarding the GFS Pride, MarineLink reports that the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore said two Singapore-registered vessels were struck by unknown projectiles, with GFS Pride sinking after catching fire. Brent stood at $105.76, down 0.19% over 24 hours, as of 15:15 UTC. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. As of 15:22 UTC, 152 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
